articles.title: Hydrogel adhesives with phase-transition-regulated tough wet adhesion and gentle removal for hemorrhage treatment and wound closure.
articles.abstract: NA: Hydrogel bioadhesives featuring rapid and robust wet adhesion are promising for hemorrhage and wound management. Nevertheless, the tight linkage may lead to secondary injury during surgical operations for subsequent removal. Herein, we develop an advanced hydrogel (PANA) with adequate wet adhesion performance (adhesion strength of 61.2 ± 9 kPa and interfacial toughness of 523 ± 36 J m-2) at body temperature and facile removal properties (adhesion strength of 5.3 ± 2.2 kPa and interfacial toughness of 50 ± 7 J m-2) at 20 °C. The main mechanism is the involvement of N-acryloyl-L-phenylalanine in hydrogel network, which not only realizes interfacial drainage and enhances matrix cohesion owing to the unique coupling structure of carboxylic and phenyl groups but also promotes thermo-triggered phase transition through regulation of hydrogen-bond-mediated hydrophobic aggregation with N-isopropylacrylamide. PANA hydrogel achieves instantaneous hemostatic sealing of diverse injuries in rabbits, and spraying normal saline (20 °C) promotes fast phase separation to enable gentle detachment for the prevention of secondary damage. Combined with cold plasma activation, the hydrogel inhibits bacterial proliferation to accelerate infected skin wound healing. Our work provides a practical solution to address the dilemma of tight wet adhesion and on-demand removal by clinically-used adhesives.

articles.title: Ultrasound-programmable poly(amino acid) nanocomposite enables synchronized metal ion-cisplatin release to overcome multidrug resistance.
articles.abstract: NA: Although immunotherapy has demonstrated remarkable clinical anti-cancer efficacy, chemotherapy remains the most widely used therapeutic modality. Multidrug resistance (MDR) remains a major barrier to platinum-based chemotherapy and is closely associated with insufficient intracellular drug accumulation, elevated antioxidant capacity, and impaired stress responsiveness in cancer cells. Here, an ultrasound (US)-programmable poly(amino acid) nanocomposite, EG-KFc20-KSA/CDDP, is developed to enable synchronized intracellular release of Fe(II) and cisplatin (CDDP) for coordinated chemoresistance reversal. Under US irradiation, EG-KFc20-KSA/CDDP accelerates the release of Fe(II) and CDDP in tumor microenvironments (TMEs), triggering overproduction of intracellular reactive oxygen species (ROS) and amplifying oxidative stress. In CDDP-resistant A549DDP lung caner cells, EG-KFc20-KSA/CDDP elevates ROS levels by 2.7-fold and reduces glutathione (GSH) levels to 31.2% of those in the Control group. Further mechanistic investigation reveals that the robust intracellular oxidative stress and associated mitochondrial damage also enhance autophagic activity, as evidenced by a marked increase in autolysosome formation. EG-KFc20-KSA/CDDP combined with US achieves an 85.3% tumor inhibition rate and prolongs the survival of A549DDP tumor-bearing mice to 61 days in vivo. This study establishes a US-programmable metal ion/chemotherapeutic co-delivery strategy that integrates oxidative stress amplification with chemotherapy and provides a mechanistically supported strategy for overcoming MDR.

articles.title: Nose-to-brain delivery of multimodal nanoregulator restores metal-redox homeostasis and protects mitochondrial integrity for triple inhibitions of neuronal death in radiation-induced brain injury.
articles.abstract: NA: Radiation-induced brain injury (RIBI) has emerged as a severe complication of cranial radiotherapy, substantially impairing patients' quality of life. Current therapies mainly rely on anti-apoptotic drugs with limited efficacy. Despite advances in understanding neuronal death in RIBI, efficient neuroprotective strategies are still lacking. Herein, we identify that beyond apoptosis, neuronal ferroptosis and cuproptosis are key drivers of RIBI. To simultaneously inhibit all three death pathways, unlike traditional approach based on small-molecular inhibitors and their combinations, we propose an innovative strategy to disrupt the vicious cycle of ROS/Fe3+/Cu2+ overload and mitochondrial dysfunction that co-drive the three cell death modalities. And a therapeutic nanodot (SPDA-SeMet) is facilely engineered by conjugating natural selenomethionine onto small-sized polydopamine nanoparticles. In RIBI mice, therapeutic outcome of SPDA-SeMet significantly outperforms neuroprotective comparator Edaravone/Dexborneol. Mechanistically, negatively-charged surface and ultrasmall size enable rapid mucus penetration and enhanced nose-to-brain delivery, and then SPDA and SeMet modules work together to restore ROS/Fe3+/Cu2+ homeostasis and preserve mitochondrial integrity in neurons via enhanced capacity in Fe3+/Cu2+ chelation, ROS scavenging, mitochondrial colocalization, thereby efficiently inhibiting neuronal apoptosis/ferroptosis/cuproptosis and inflammation. Our findings establish an essential role of neuronal ferroptosis/cuproptosis/apoptosis in RIBI pathogenesis, and provides a therapeutic nanoplatform regulating complex pathological processes for targeted therapy.

articles.title: First use of a woven allogeneic vascular graft made of cell-assembled extracellular matrix (CAM) as an arteriovenous shunt in sheep: a pilot study.
articles.abstract: NA: Reliable vascular access is vital for patients undergoing hemodialysis. Current arteriovenous shunts (AVS) made of expanded polytetrafluoroethylene (ePTFE) are prone to thrombosis, intimal hyperplasia, and infections. To overcome these limitations, biological Tissue-Engineered Vascular Grafts (TEVGs) were produced by weaving threads made from Cell-Assembled extracellular Matrix (CAM), i.e., extracellular matrix produced by ovine fibroblasts in culture. The woven TEVGs were designed with a 6 mm internal diameter and beveled ends to facilitate use as an AVS. They had a burst pressure (3069 ± 546 mmHg) and a compliance (4.4 ± 0.5%/100 mmHg) closer to those of native blood vessels than ePTFE prostheses. Woven TEVGs were implanted as carotid-jugular AVS in sheep and compared to ePTFE controls in a bilateral model (n = 8 animals). Grafts were easily punctured with 16G hemodialysis needles once at 4 weeks without loss of structural integrity or hemorrhagic complications. Overall TEVGs patency was 100%, while it was 87.5% for ePTFE grafts (n = 8). Histological analysis revealed an inflammatory response that decreased between 4 and 8 weeks. A luminal neotissue was observed at 8 weeks with smooth muscle cells and localized endothelialization. Localized calcification of CAM was observed and appeared to be correlated with high tissue compaction. This proof-of-concept study demonstrates the feasibility of using a completely biological TEVG made from woven CAM as an AVS in an allogeneic large animal model. Future studies are needed to understand and avoid the never-before-observed calcification of the CAM in a large animal model, as well as to determine longer-term outcomes.

articles.title: Bio-orthogonally functionalized biomimetic nanoreactors suppress lung cancer stem-like cells by triggering a self-amplifying endoplasmic reticulum-mitochondria stress loop.
articles.abstract: NA: The compensatory signal transmission between the endoplasmic reticulum (ER) and mitochondria maintains the survival of lung cancer stem cells (LCSCs). This study designed a bio-orthogonally functionalized biomimetic nanoreactor to dissociate this protective crosstalk and induce a self-amplifying stress feedback loop. By integrating an N-cadherin-targeting aptamer with tumor membrane masking technology, this nanoreactor achieves enhanced specificity for LCSCs targeting. The nanoreactor is loaded with the photosensitizer TAPP and bortezomib (BTZ). Upon laser irradiation, TAPP generates reactive oxygen species (ROS) locally, rapidly collapsing the mitochondrial membrane potential and inducing oxidative injury. Concurrently, BTZ inhibits the proteasome, blocking the degradation of ubiquitinated proteins and triggering acute ER stress, which promotes Ca2+ release into mitochondria and further exacerbates mitochondrial damage. In turn, damaged mitochondria release mitochondrial DNA (mtDNA), aggravating ER dysfunction and establishing a self-amplifying vicious cycle between the ER and mitochondria that progressively escalates cellular damage. Additionally, treatment was accompanied by reduced STAT3 phosphorylation and decreased expression of stemness-associated markers, alongside ER-mitochondrial dysfunction and enhanced cytotoxicity in stem-like cells.

articles.title: FGF2-engineered extracellular vesicles loaded in an ECM-mimetic hydrogel promote wound healing and attenuate scar formation via immunomodulation and enhanced neurovascular responses.
articles.abstract: NA: Impaired wound healing in diabetes is primarily driven by persistent inflammation and neurovascular dysfunction, frequently leading to aberrant tissue remodeling and pathological scarring. Extracellular vesicles of adipose-derived mesenchymal stem cells (ADSC-EVs) have therapeutic potential but limited tissue-specific efficacy. Fibroblast growth factor 2 (FGF2) promotes angiogenesis and nerve repair but suffers from a short half-life that limits its clinical application. Given the low endogenous expression of FGF2 in ADSCs and its short half-life in vivo, here, we engineered FGF2-functionalized EVs (EV-FGF2) by lentiviral transduction of ADSCs and incorporated them into a click chemistry-crosslinked recombinant collagen/hyaluronic acid hydrogel (CH/EV-FGF2) to enable sustained release and extracellular matrix-mimetic support. In vitro, EV-FGF2 promoted macrophage polarization toward a reparative M2 phenotype, enhanced angiogenesis and axonal outgrowth. In vivo, the CH/EV-FGF2 hydrogel accelerated wound closure in a diabetic mouse wound model, attenuated early inflammation, increased vascular (CD31) and neuronal (βIII-tubulin/Tuj1) markers, promoted neurovascular-associated responses, and attenuated scar formation in a rabbit ear model. In conclusion, this study developed an engineered EV-FGF2 hydrogel system that addresses multiple pathological aspects of diabetic wounds, offering a promising cell-free therapeutic strategy for tissue repair.

articles.title: Spatial bridges of hierarchical scaffolds orchestrate MSCs/SCs interaction for bone regeneration.
articles.abstract: NA: The spatiotemporal distribution of multiple cells and their interactions with extracellular matrix in three-dimensional microenvironments play a critical role in regulating cell behaviors and modulating tissue development and regeneration. Preparation of hierarchical structural scaffolds for multicellular crosstalk in tissue engineering holds great significance. Here, inspired conceptually by the idea of "magpie bridge", biomimetic hierarchical multi-channel scaffolds, serving as "spatial bridges" to orchestrate multicellular spatiotemporal interactions have been proposed for innervated bone regeneration. Hierarchical multi-channel structures facilitate the mutual migration and energy metabolism activities of mesenchymal stem cells (MSCs) and Schwann cells (SCs), thereby enhancing their specific differentiation. Transcriptomic analysis revealed that MSCs/SCs cross-talk mediated by cytokine-cytokine receptor interactions, including the activation of multiple neurogenesis/osteogenesis-related signaling pathways. In rabbit bone defect model, SCs-laden hierarchical multi-channel scaffolds constructed a neuro-inductive metabolism-activated microenvironment, thereby achieving 3.24-fold increase in bone regeneration and 2.29-fold increase in neuro-vascular networks reconstruction compared to traditional bioceramic scaffolds in the core defects region at 12-week post-surgery, respectively. Therefore, this study introduces an exceptional concept that biomimetic hierarchical scaffolds serve as "spatial bridges" for accelerating multicellular spatiotemporal interactions of complex tissue and organ regeneration, opening new avenues for designing next-generation regenerative biomaterials.

articles.title: Charge-neutralized anti-swelling hydrogels enable mechano-curvature-coupled microphysiological system.
articles.abstract: NA: Curvature topography and mechanical stimulation are key biophysical cues in the tissue microenvironment that play critical roles in regulating cell behavior. However, the stable construction of curved structures and the application of dynamic mechanical loading in ultrasoft biomaterials remain challenging, limiting the reconstruction of microenvironments for soft tissues such as the lung. Here, we propose a charge-neutralization anti-swelling hydrogel strategy. By introducing LiCl, Li+ ions electrostatically shield and coordinate with fixed negative charges, thereby suppressing the Donnan effect to inhibit hydrogel swelling and enhance structural stability. The resulting hydrogel exhibits a tunable Young's modulus ranging from 1.12 to 339.79 kPa. Combined with three-dimensional (3D) printing, biomimetic curved structures with curvatures ranging from 10-4 to 4 × 10-2 μm-1 were stably fabricated. Integration with a stretching driver further enabled controllable cyclic stretching (0∼40%), establishing a microphysiological system that couples curvature topography with mechanical cues and recapitulates the physiological and pathological parameters of multiple tissues. Curvature topography and mechanical stimulation significantly influenced tissue phenotypes, including surfactant secretion, proliferation, and migration, as well as drug sensitivity. This work provides a general design strategy for reconstructing complex tissue microenvironments and establishes a more physiologically relevant platform for investigating tissue development, disease mechanisms, and drug responses.

articles.title: Heptamethine cyanines serve as photocaged Michael electrophiles for spatiotemporal GPX4 inhibition and ferroptosis immunotherapy.
articles.abstract: NA: Inhibiting glutathione peroxidase 4 (GPX4) to induce ferroptosis has emerged as a crucial strategy to circumvent drug resistance. However, conventional GPX4 inhibitors, typically α-chloroacetamides, show limitations in the stability and targetability required for drug development. Here we uncover that heptamethine cyanines (Cy7) function as photocaged Michael electrophiles, enabling spatiotemporal GPX4 inhibition and ferroptosis induction with submicromolar to nanomolar potencies against both parental and drug-resistant cancer cells. The strong phototoxicity originates from the optimized electrophilicity window of the photo-uncaged Michael electrophiles, which enables selective alkylation of GPX4 selenocysteine over glutathione (GSH), thereby circumventing cellular GSH detoxification. Furthermore, the structural tunability of Cy7 dyes enables on-demand fabrication of cancer cell-specific GPX4 inhibitors, as exemplified by an enzyme-activatable Cy7 prodrug that selectively killed cancer cells in primary tumors under photoirradiation while eliciting systemic antitumor immunity to suppress distant tumors. This work establishes a new paradigm for GPX4 inhibitor development and repurposes conventional Cy7 imaging scaffolds as anticancer agents.

articles.title: Energy band tunable piezoelectric nanozyme heterojunction toward cancer synergistic catalytic therapy.
articles.abstract: NA: Piezoelectric catalytic therapy (PCT) based on piezoelectric semiconductors provides a new approach for cancer therapy. Various researches have explored the construction of heterojunction structures with nanozymes to strengthen PCT effect via accelerating electron transfer kinetics and synergistic nanozyme catalysis therapy (NCT). However, limited by the fixed energy band structure of nanozymes, the selectable piezoelectric semiconductors and nanozymes with matched energy levels are few. In this work, Cu2+ engineered nanozyme MIL-100 (Fe) was self-assembled on the surface of piezoelectric material BaTiO3 (BTO) to obtain BaTiO3@MIL-100 (Fe, Cu) (BTO@Fe-Cu) nanoparticles (NPs) with flexible heterojunction types, which presented synergetic NCT and PCT effect. Theoretical calculations revealed that Cu2+ introduced a new 3d orbital in the Fe-O structure, which altered the charge transfer pathways and enhanced the dual-enzyme activity of MIL-100 (Fe). Lattice distortion further modulated the valence band gap and transformed the heterostructure from type-Ⅰ to type-S for high electron-hole separation efficiency. BTO@Fe-Cu NPs fundamentally intensified the efficiency of NCT and PCT, which synergistically activated the ferroptosis/cuproptosis pathways. Moreover, scRNA-seq analysis indicated treatment-associated changes in immune-cell composition and transcriptional states. Together with the immunophenotyping results, these findings supported the potential of the piezoelectric nanozyme for the immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment (TME) regulation.

articles.title: Polysaccharide-confined polyaniline nanocomplexes reprogram pyrimidine metabolism for synergistic photothermal tumor ablation.
articles.abstract: NA: Polyaniline (PANI) is a promising near-infrared (NIR) photothermal agent, yet its aggregation propensity and lack of intrinsic metabolic regulatory functions restrict its in vivo antitumor application. To overcome these limitations, we engineered a biocompatible curdlan/fucoidan/polyaniline (CFP) ternary inclusion complex via a nanoconfined in-situ polymerization strategy. Utilizing the hydrophobic helical cavity of curdlan as a nano-reactor effectively regulates PANI chain growth, yielding monodispersed nanorods with superior aqueous dispersion stability. Fucoidan serves a dual role as an efficient dispersant and a potent metabolic modulator implicated in pyrimidine pathway suppression. Mechanistically, CFP enters lung adenocarcinoma cells predominantly via macropinocytosis, accounting for ∼44-47% of total internalization, with clathrin- and caveolae-mediated routes contributing only marginally. Multi-omics profiling reveals that fucoidan preferentially modulates pyrimidine metabolism, with significant down-regulation of the core enzymes TK1, DTYMK, and CDA observed at both transcriptomic and protein levels. This metabolic suppression compromises DNA damage repair capacity, rendering the massive ROS accumulation and severe DNA damage induced by PANI-based photothermal therapy largely irreversible and achieving remarkable synergistic antitumor efficacy. Bioinformatic analysis further links these metabolic genes to T cell exhaustion and immune microenvironment remodeling. In vivo, the CFP + NIR regimen exhibits prominent tumor accumulation, potent growth inhibition, and prolonged survival. Crucially, comprehensive toxicological assessments in immunocompetent mice-including hematological, serum biochemical, and histological analyses-confirm the excellent systemic biosafety of CFP. This work presents a promising strategy coupling natural polysaccharide-mediated metabolic intervention with photothermal ablation for precise tumor therapy.

articles.title: Use of a c-Met-targeting aptamer-drug conjugate for efficient therapy in both primary and metastatic uveal melanoma.
articles.abstract: NA: Uveal melanoma (UM), the most common primary intraocular malignancy in adults, is associated with a high risk of metastasis, recurrence, and irreversible vision loss. However, current therapeutic options remain limited by insufficient efficacy and poor vision preservation. Building upon the molecular design of SL1-MMAE, a c-Met-targeting aptamer-drug conjugate (ApDC), here we investigate its potential translational application as a targeted therapeutic strategy for both primary and metastatic UM. SL1-MMAE exhibits high binding specificity, rapid cellular internalization, and potent cytotoxicity toward UM cells in vitro. In vivo, SL1-MMAE effectively suppresses tumor growth in both subcutaneous xenograft and liver metastasis models, significantly prolonging survival. Notably, in an orthotopic intraocular UM model, a single intravitreal injection of SL1-MMAE induces robust tumor regression without detectable ocular toxicity at the therapeutic dose. The small molecular size of the ApDC enables superior tumor penetration and reduced retention from non-target ocular tissues. These features are particularly advantageous within the confined intraocular environment, leading to enhanced therapeutic efficacy with improved safety. Compared with the clinically advanced c-Met antibody-drug conjugate (ADC) ABBV-399, the ApDC demonstrates superior antitumor activity and ocular biocompatibility for intraocular UM therapy. Nevertheless, as a preclinical study, further safety, pharmacokinetic and translational studies are warranted to better define the clinical potential of SL1-MMAE. Collectively, these findings establish c-Met-targeting ApDCs as a promising platform for the treatment of both primary and metastatic UM, offering a vision-preserving therapeutic strategy with potent antitumor efficacy and favorable safety profiles.

articles.title: Endothelium-targeted myc silencing suppresses pathological ocular neovascularization.
articles.abstract: NA: Ocular neovascularization (NV) causes blindness, yet anti-VEGF therapy has limited efficacy. Myc controls endothelial cell (EC) proliferation and activation, however, its pathological role in ocular NV and therapeutic value remain unclear. In this study, we found that Myc was markedly upregulated in neovascular ECs (NV-ECs). Mechanistically, glycolytic reprogramming drove the hexosamine biosynthetic pathway (HBP), promoting Myc O-GlcNAcylation, which stabilized Myc protein. Endothelial-specific Myc knockout significantly suppressed EC proliferation, thereby alleviating NV progression and preserving visual function. To target Myc therapeutically, we engineered an endothelium targeted, cell membrane hybridized lipid nanoparticle encapsulating Myc siRNA (Lip@siMyc). This system achieved homotypic targeting, vitreal penetration, and sustained Myc gene silencing, and markedly inhibited ocular NV in mice. Notably, Lip@siMyc showed efficacy comparable to aflibercept, and combined treatment produced enhanced anti angiogenic effects. In summary, our findings establish the glycolysis/HBP/Myc axis as a critical regulator of EC proliferation and highlight endothelial Myc blockade as a promising therapeutic strategy for ocular NV.

articles.title: Orchestrating adaptive homeostasis on bioprosthetic valves: a metal-polyphenol hydrogel armor for integrated immunomodulation and endothelialization.
articles.abstract: NA: With the advancement of transcatheter valve replacement technology, bioprosthetic heart valves (BHVs) are being increasingly used in the clinical treatment of valvular diseases. However, current BHVs fail to concurrently resist thrombosis, modulate the immune and redox homeostasis in response to complex host-biomaterial interactions, leading to premature degeneration and shortened lifespan. Herein, we constructed an endothelial layer-inspired armor for BHV by fusing metal-polyphenol drug network (MPN) nanoparticle with immune/redox regulation functions and vascular endothelial glycocalyx-like layer that serve as passive defense and endothelialization scaffolds. The coating established a biomimetic endothelial defense barrier that resisted the deposition of blood components on BHVs while acting as a scaffold for endothelialization. The MPN nanoparticle fabricated through the self-assembly of Epigallocatechin-3-gallate, curcumin, and Cu2+ was anchored to endow the BHV with free-radical-scavenging capability, immunomodulatory activity and endothelialization-promoting potential. The overexpressed reactive oxygen species were scavenged and the local inflammation responses were downregulated through immune and inflammatory response pathways. This not only maintained homeostasis at the BHV bio-interface but also created a pro-endothelialization microenvironment that favors the adhesion and growth of endothelial cells. Additionally, the coating catalyzed the releasing of NO to promote the endothelialization through PI3K/AKT/mTOR pathway. The combined advantages of nanoparticles and glycocalyx-like hydrogel, which integrate antithrombotic, immunomodulatory, antioxidant, endothelialization-promoting, and anti-calcification effects, provided a promising strategy to address the critical challenge of BHV degeneration.

articles.title: Engineering hypoactivated platelet-derived coating to decouple thrombosis for vascular regeneration.
articles.abstract: NA: The clinical performance of intravascular stents remains limited by thrombotic complications and delayed vascular healing. While cell membrane-based coatings have been explored to recapitulate native biointerfaces, achieving simultaneous hemocompatibility and pro-regenerative functionality remains challenging due to the intrinsic thrombogenicity of platelet-derived materials. Here, we propose a brand-new hypoactivated platelet-derived coating (hPLC) by sequentially assembling fibrin networks and low-activated platelets, followed by controlled lysis to remove pro-thrombotic components. This approach preserves the structural and biointerfacial features of platelet membrane while decoupling thrombogenic activity from regenerative functionality. The resulting hPLC endows materials with reduced protein adsorption, suppressed coagulation, and attenuated inflammatory responses. Transcriptomic analysis further reveals that hPLC enhances endothelial compatibility through coordinated regulation of anti-apoptotic, cytoskeletal remodeling, and angiogenic pathways. In vivo stent implantation studies demonstrate that hPLC-coated stents provide a pro-regenerative microenvironment, significantly accelerating re-endothelialization while inhibiting neointimal hyperplasia and peri-strut inflammation. These findings establish a bioinspired and clinically translatable strategy for engineering multifunctional vascular interfaces from readily available blood components, offering a versatile platform for the surface engineering of vascular devices.

articles.title: Mitochondria-protective polysaccharide augments burn wound repair through immunometabolic reprogramming.
articles.abstract: NA: Effective wound healing requires coordinated extracellular matrix (ECM) deposition, immune regulation, and metabolic adaptation-processes governed by fibroblast mitochondria. Conventional burn therapies fail to address the mitochondrial dysfunction that impedes tissue regeneration. Here, we show that colanic acid (CA), a microbial-derived exopolysaccharide, acts as a mitochondrial-protecting biomaterial that accelerates burn repair by restoring immuno-metabolic crosstalk. In a murine deep second-degree burn model, CA enhanced wound closure 3.1-fold over controls, reduced reactive oxidative species by 54%, and increased mature collagen deposition by 193%. Mechanistically, CA undergoes intracellular internalization with the assistance of the membrane receptor TLR4 and maintains mitochondrial integrity, evidenced by restored cristae ultrastructure, a 1.4-fold increase in oxidative phosphorylation flux, and a 1.5-fold elevation in ATP production-effects abolished upon silencing the mitochondrial regulator Thap11. Bulk RNA-seq indicated that CA reshaped the wound immune landscape by driving macrophage recruitment and M2 polarization via mitochondrial metabolic reprogramming. By synchronizing mitochondrial rescue with immune-guided ECM remodeling, CA outperformed hyaluronic acid dressings in wound closure and extracellular matrix remodeling.The preliminary translational proof-of-concept of CA was confirmed in a Bama minipig model of deep second-degree burn wound, where it enhanced re-epithelialization, angiogenesis, and tissue perfusion. Together, these findings suggest that CA is a multifunctional polysaccharide with mitochondrial protective effects capable of addressing the multifaceted pathology of burn wounds across species.

articles.title: Protection against osteoporosis by an osteo-immune niche through FOXP3-dependent systemic immunoregulation.
articles.abstract: NA: Osteo-immune diseases require immunoregulatory strategies that suppress pathological inflammation and restore the balance between immunity and bone remodeling. Here, we demonstrate that a subcutaneously implanted bone-mimetic scaffold generates an ectopic osteo-immune niche that confers systemic protection against osteoporosis. Following implantation, the scaffold elicited a structured foreign body response that organized recruited host cells into a compartmentalized immune microenvironment. And this osteo-immune niche is associated with regulatory immune features, including a FOXP3+ regulatory T cell (Treg)-enriched profile. In an osteoporosis model, this approach was linked to attenuation of systemic bone loss together with immunological changes consistent with an increased Treg population, suggesting that local niche engineering can influence whole-body skeletal health. Collectively, these findings support bone mimetic, immune instructive biomaterial scaffold as a potential therapeutic platform for osteo-immune disorders without the need for complex cell processing.

articles.title: Stress-relaxing and ROS-scavenging hydrogel microspheres restore osteoimmune homeostasis for bone regeneration under mechanoinflammatory conditions.
articles.abstract: NA: Periodontitis drives alveolar bone loss, tooth mobility, and even tooth loss. Although orthodontic treatment can reposition compromised teeth and extend their functional lifespan, orthodontic tooth movement in patients with periodontitis occurs within a mechanoinflammatory microenvironment, where mechanical forces and persistent inflammation synergistically disrupt alveolar bone homeostasis and compromise stem-cell-mediated repair, culminating in bone loss. Breaking this vicious cycle demands a therapy that can simultaneously buffer physical stress and neutralize biochemical insults. Here we report injectable, stress-relaxing, and ROS-scavenging hydrogel microspheres that function as a protective microniche for dental follicle stem cells (DFSCs). Constructed from dopamine-modified hyaluronic acid and phenylboronic acid-modified gelatin, these viscoelastic microspheres rapidly dissipate mechanical stress while their catechol moieties mitigate oxidative damage. Under a combined mechanoinflammatory challenge, the microspheres preserved DFSC viability, stemness, osteogenic potential, and immunomodulatory function. Transcriptomic analysis revealed that the microspheres rescued the expression of the DNA repair enzyme OGG1, thereby preventing oxidative DNA damage and suppressing the downstream NF-κB inflammatory cascade. In a murine model of periodontitis-associated orthodontic tooth movement, DFSCs-loaded microspheres not only prevented bone loss but also restored a pro-regenerative osteoimmune homeostasis. Together, this study presents a viscoelastic and redox-active biomaterial-based strategy to safeguard stem cell function and restore osteoimmune balance in mechanically and immunologically challenged tissues.

articles.title: Pathology-adaptive composite hydrogel for efficient suppression of autoimmune uveitis: disrupting bidirectional crosstalk between immune cells and blood-retinal barriers.
articles.abstract: NA: Autoimmune uveitis (AU) is a sight-threatening intraocular inflammatory disorder with limited safe therapeutic options. Pathological progression of experimental autoimmune uveitis (EAU) follows a temporally staged pattern: early disease onset is driven by aberrant microglial activation that initiates blood-retinal barrier (BRB) disruption, while advanced stages are characterized by reactive oxygen species accumulation and robust infiltration of pathogenic CD44+ immune cells. Capitalizing on this stage-dependent pathological feature, we design a thermosensitive poly (dl-lactide)-b-poly (ethylene glycol)-b-poly (dl-lactide) (PLEL) composite hydrogel (Mino&nanoCur@PLEL) co-loaded with minocycline (Mino) and CD44-targeted curcumin nanoparticles (nanoCur). The engineered platform delivers programmable biphasic drug release to implement stepwise immunomodulation, matching the dynamic EAU pathological process. Rapidly released Mino suppresses early microglial overactivation and stabilizes retinal innate immune homeostasis, whereas sustained nanoCur release enables precise targeting of proinflammatory CD44+ macrophages to block inflammatory cascades and protect BRB structure. In EAU rats, single subconjunctival hydrogel administration efficiently restrains inflammatory deterioration by disrupting the bidirectional proinflammatory interplay between myeloid immune cells and BRB-resident endothelial/retinal pigment epithelial cells, remodeling retinal immune microenvironments and restoring both inner and outer BRB integrity. This pathology-adaptive dual-target immunotherapeutic system offers a translatable precision strategy for AU treatment.

articles.title: Engineering framework-derived carbon enables effective near-infrared photocatalytic hydrogen peroxide generation for cascade cancer therapy.
articles.abstract: NA: Hydrogen peroxide (H2O2)-mediated catalysis is key to oxidative chemical transformations and catalytic cancer therapies. However, its efficiency is limited by the lack of controllable catalytic systems capable of selectively driving two-electron oxygen reduction under physiologically relevant conditions. Herein, photocatalytic H2O2 generation in carbon systems was discovered to be governed by programmable electronic structures rather than material composition. By exploiting a framework-derived transformation, a series of carbon nanostructures were constructed with continuously adjustable electronic states, which enabled correlation between electronic configuration and photocatalytic behavior. Thus, a non-monotonic dependence of activity on graphitization degree was identified, where an intermediate semi-graphitized phase maximizes near-infrared (NIR) absorption, charge separation, and selective two-electron oxygen reduction. In contrast, insufficient conjugation limits excitation efficiency, while excessive delocalization accelerates carrier recombination, defining an electronic-structure window for optimal catalysis. This electronically optimized structure enables NIR-driven H2O2 generation without sacrificial agents, which further couples with Fe2+-mediated Fenton reactions and hole-driven glutathione depletion to achieve a self-amplifying redox cascade for cancer therapy. The as-obtained system achieves efficient oxidative transformation in vitro and significant tumor suppression in vivo. These findings suggest an electronic-structure-associated paradigm for carbon-based photocatalysis and provide a generalizable strategy for modulating reaction selectivity and efficiency in metal-free systems.

articles.title: Pharmacologically programmed tolerogenic dendritic cell membrane-coated nanoparticles for CCR7-dependent lymphoid organ targeting in transplantation.
articles.abstract: NA: Secondary lymphoid organs (SLOs) are critical sites for alloimmune activation and attractive targets for transplantation immunotherapy. However, current cell membrane-based targeting strategies face a fundamental trade-off between low immunogenicity and efficient SLO homing, limiting their therapeutic potential. To resolve this functional trade-off, we developed a biomimetic delivery system (PD-DmRK) by coating self-assembled RapaLink-1 (RK) nanoparticles with cell membranes derived from PP242 and docosahexaenoic acid (DHA)-induced tolerogenic dendritic cells (TolDCs). Compared with conventional tolerogenic induction strategies, PP242/DHA preserved low immunogenicity and markedly increased CCR7 expression, thereby improving SLO targeting. Mechanistically, PP242 and DHA cooperatively activated the transcription factor USF2, which directly bound to the Ccr7 promoter and transcriptionally upregulated Ccr7 expression. Consequently, PD-DmRK exhibited enhanced accumulation in SLOs, reduced hepatic and renal sequestration, and significantly prolonged skin and cardiac allograft survival. High-dimensional spectral flow cytometry and single-cell transcriptomic analyses further indicated that PD-DmRK treatment was associated with enrichment of Ccr9-expressing plasmacytoid dendritic cells and regulatory T cells, accompanied by reduced cytotoxic T-cell responses. Overall, PD-DmRK provides a TolDC membrane platform in which the USF2-CCR7 axis links immunoregulatory activity with CCR7-dependent SLO targeting, supporting its potential for targeted immunotherapy in transplantation.

articles.title: Biomaterial thrombosis-on-a-chip: Real-time visualisation of biomaterial thrombosis at clinical heparin levels.
articles.abstract: NA: Blood-contacting medical device thrombosis causes device failure, embolism and bleeding due to reliance on anti-thrombotic drugs. The interplay between biological, material and flow parameters in medical device thrombosis remains poorly understood. Importantly, tools to evaluate acute, dynamic thrombotic events on materials in real-time are lacking, impacting the successful development and translation of new anti-thrombotic materials. We developed a biomaterial thrombosis-on-a-chip model to evaluate acute material thrombogenicity in real-time using human whole blood, mimicking clinical heparin doses (0.5-5 U/mL) and shear rates (50-2000 s-1). System validation showed expected platelet adhesion on hydrophilic glass and platelet passivation and detachment at increasing shears on hydrophobic silicone. For the first time, we characterised fibrin events on materials, finding a shear dependent decrease on glass but not silicone, pre-coating materials with albumin abolished fibrin on silicone but not glass, and inhibition of FXIIa reduced but did not abolish fibrin on either material. More and larger fibrin events (aggregation and channel occlusion) occurred at 0.5 U/mL compared to 5 U/mL heparin, and the heparin level did not affect platelet adhesion dynamics. Glass showed the most severe fibrin events, followed by polyvinyl chloride (PVC) > silicone > polycarbonate. Most fibrin events occurred in association with platelets and although platelets were P-selectin positive, very few platelets were procoagulant (P-selectin and Annexin V positive). This clinically relevant, biomaterial thrombosis-on-a-chip model could allow biomaterial thrombosis mechanism elucidation and fast-track evaluation and development of anti-thrombotic materials to improve medical device function and reduce adverse thrombotic and bleeding patient outcomes.

articles.title: Transcription activator-like effector base editing delivered by a targeted lipid nanoparticle for therapy of lung cancer.
articles.abstract: NA: Lung cancer is the leading cause of cancer-related deaths worldwide. Among them, non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) accounts for approximately 85% of all cases, while the mutation of KRAS oncogene plays a crucial role in its formation and metastasis. Here, we report a transcription activator-like effector (TALE) base editor that can accurately identify KRAS gene under the guide of TALE and sgRNA, convert C base to T base, thereby generating a stop codon and blocking the expression of KRAS. Besides, a targeted TALE base editing lipid nanoparticle (targeted TALE LNP) is developed by rationally designing with cancer-targeted EGFR peptide. The targeted TALE LNP exhibits a base editing effect, cancer targeting, and remarkable therapy efficacy in NSCLC cancer-bearing mice. In conclusion, the targeted TALE LNP has the potential to treat lung cancer with KRAS gene mutation through an approach of transcription activator-like effector base editing.

articles.title: Piezoelectric electroporation potentiates high-frequency irreversible electroporation for enhanced prostate cancer eradication.
articles.abstract: NA: Residual tumor cell persistence remains a critical unresolved barrier limiting focal therapy such as high-frequency irreversible electroporation (H-FIRE) for prostate cancer. In this study, we identified DNA damage repair as the central mechanism governing the reversible survival of residual cells after H-FIRE. By exploiting the transient membrane permeability of these residual cells following H-FIRE, we engineered a piezoelectrically active nanomaterial, BOIS. Exogenous electric pulses generated by H-FIRE enhance tumor membrane permeabilization, thereby facilitating the intracellular delivery of BOIS and promoting its efficient penetration into residual malignant cells. Upon ultrasound activation, BOIS induces surface charge separation and electron migration, producing an intrinsic electric field accompanied by reactive oxygen species (ROS). This dual mechanism cascade simultaneously inflicts endogenous electric field-mediated electroporation damage on both cellular and nuclear membranes and imposes lethal oxidative stress, thereby converting reversibly injured residual cells into an irreversible death trajectory. Consequently, residual tumor cells with damage repair capacity are converted from a reversibly injured state to irreversible lethal damage. Unlike conventional combination therapies, this study pioneered a new therapeutic paradigm in which the focal ablation procedure functions as a nanomaterial delivery mechanism, thereby establishing a self-reinforcing therapeutic loop. This strategy markedly amplified the therapeutic efficacy of H-FIRE and enhanced the eradication of residual tumor cells. Collectively, these findings establish a groundbreaking therapeutic paradigm for eliminating residual disease following focal ablation.

articles.title: Programming a pro-regenerative microenvironment via a photocurable albumin-matrix hydrogel for hepatic tissue reconstitution.
articles.abstract: NA: Liver tissue engineering (LTE) is constrained by poor hepatocyte survival and functional deterioration after transplantation. A central challenge is to support hepatocyte growth and expansion in vitro while preserving polarity and specialized hepatic functions. Graft immunogenicity and surgical intervention trigger inflammation and immune rejection, further compromising transplanted cell survival and performance. Limited vascularization also restricts graft survival, function, and expansion in vivo. Here, we developed a photocurable biomimetic composite hydrogel by combining bovine serum albumin methacrylate (BSA-MA) with decellularized liver extracellular matrix (dECM) derived from α1,3-galactosyltransferase knockout (GTKO) Bama miniature pigs, and used it to encapsulate primary hepatocyte spheroids to construct functional engineered hepatic tissue (EHT). The BSA-MA-dECM hydrogel exhibited favorable physicochemical properties, cytocompatibility, and histocompatibility, while sustaining and enhancing hepatocyte viability, function, and polarity. It also reduced inflammatory responses, promoted macrophage polarization toward the M2 phenotype, and stimulated angiogenesis through VEGF and FGF upregulation as well as PI3K-AKT pathway activation. Thus, the hydrogel established a pro-regenerative microenvironment that supported hepatocyte expansion and graft vascularization. Following implantation into the omentum of rats with CCl4-induced liver injury, the EHT underwent rapid vascularization and showed robust expansion in vivo. It alleviated liver injury, collagen deposition, and fibrosis, while transcriptomic analysis revealed enhanced metabolic repair and cytoprotective programs along with the suppression of inflammatory and fibrotic pathways. Overall, these findings identify BSA-MA-dECM as a versatile photocurable hydrogel for hepatocyte delivery and provide a broadly applicable strategy that integrates immune modulation with vascular induction for scalable EHT construction and liver regenerative therapy.

articles.title: Balancing localized and charge-transfer excited states in Dithieno[3,2-b:2',3'-d]pyrrole-based NIR-II AIE photosensitizers for low power phototheranostics.
articles.abstract: NA: Photodynamic therapy (PDT) is limited by the shallow tissue penetration of visible-light excitation and the hypoxic tumor microenvironment, while effective photothermal therapy (PTT) and PDT/PTT synergistic therapy remain difficult to achieve under clinically approved laser power. Here, we report a progressive donor-acceptor (D-A) intensification strategy that, counterintuitively, reveals a critical excited-state phase transition from a charge-transfer (CT)-dominated regime to a balanced localized-excitation (LE)/CT hybrid. At this tipping point, the inherent orthogonality between radiative decay, intersystem crossing, and thermal dissipation is synergistically breached. This process concurrently unlocks NIR-II emission, oxygen-independent Type-I photodynamic activity, and an exceptional photothermal conversion efficiency of 87.4%. Such tri-functional synergy is conspicuously absent in conventional D-A systems with either weak or excessive D-A interactions. Quantitative structure-property relationship analysis establishes the LE/CT composition ratio as a predictive descriptor for triplet-state reactivity, enabling rational rather than trial and error optimization. Guided by this paradigm, the optimal photosensitizer achieves potent antitumor efficacy under mild 808 nm irradiation (0.33 W/cm2), effectively decoupling therapeutic potency from reliance on high-intensity laser exposure. This work thus shifts phototheranostic design from discrete molecular screening to excited-state composition engineering, offering a conceptually transformative roadmap for safe and efficient NIR-II phototheranostics.

articles.title: Cell-enriched granular bioinks enable vascular integration and endometrial repair.
articles.abstract: NA: 3D bioprinting is essential for constructing functional tissue mimics but remains challenging due to the difficulty of simultaneously achieving adequate cell-cell interactions and appropriate biomaterial support. Here, we introduce a cell-driven clustering strategy that assembles hydrogel microparticles into cell-rich aggregates, in which cells occupy the interstitial spaces and establish pre-organized cellular interactions prior to printing. The cell volume fraction and aggregate size are tunable by microparticle properties and cell type. When applied to digital light processing 3D bioprinting, the cell-clustered granular bioink exhibits high printability while maintaining high cell density and viability. Importantly, preserving pre-established cellular organization translates into enhanced function, including improved stemness maintenance and a more regenerative paracrine profile characterized by increased angiogenic factor secretion and reduced inflammatory signaling. In vivo, implanted constructs show improved cell retention, successful vascular integration with host circulation, and significantly enhanced endometrial repair with reduced fibrosis. These results establish cell-clustered granular bioinks as a generalizable biofabrication strategy for engineering transplantable artificial tissues.

articles.title: An injectable ROS-responsive natural drug self-delivery hydrogel relieves neuropathic pain by remodeling DRG macrophage-mediated neuroinflammation.
articles.abstract: NA: Neuropathic pain remains a major clinical challenge owing to complex neuroimmune mechanisms and limited disease-modifying therapies. Neuroinflammation within the dorsal root ganglion (DRG), particularly macrophage infiltration and pro-inflammatory polarization, is a key driver of sensory neuronal sensitization and pain persistence. Here, we report an injectable reactive oxygen species (ROS)-responsive natural drug self-delivery hydrogel for localized and sustained treatment of neuropathic pain. Single-cell transcriptomic reanalysis revealed marked macrophage accumulation in injured DRGs, accompanied by M1-like polarization and aberrant phosphatidylinositol 3-kinase (PI3K)-Akt activation. Mechanism-guided virtual screening identified glycyrrhizic acid (GA), a bioactive natural product, as a promising PI3K-targeting candidate. To improve local bioavailability, GA was engineered into a 1,4-phenylenediboronic acid (1,4-PBA)-functionalized self-assembled hydrogel, termed GA-PBA-GA (GPG), through dynamic boronate ester bonds and non-covalent interactions. The GPG hydrogel exhibited injectability, self-healing, biodegradability, biocompatibility, and inflammation-associated ROS-triggered GA release. In vitro, GPG suppressed PI3K-Akt signaling, reduced pro-inflammatory macrophage activation, and promoted M1-to-M2 repolarization. In a rat model of L5 spinal nerve ligation-induced neuropathic pain, peri-DRG administration alleviated mechanical and thermal hypersensitivity, improved gait and electrophysiological function, reduced DRG macrophage-mediated neuroinflammation, and attenuated spinal microglial activation. This ROS-responsive natural drug self-delivery hydrogel provides a minimally invasive strategy for remodeling DRG neuroinflammation and achieving sustained relief of neuropathic pain through localized drug delivery.

articles.title: Magnesium-loaded anisotropic hydrogel promotes tendon healing via combined immunomodulation and collagen remodeling.
articles.abstract: NA: Poor tendon healing remains a challenging clinical problem. An ideal repair scaffold should create a favorable microenvironment for dynamic regeneration, including inflammation control, cell proliferation promotion, revascularization, and collagen remodeling. Herein, a dynamic self-adaptive hydrogel scaffold was developed using non-covalent crosslinking and pre-stretching-induced alignment. This biomimetic scaffold integrates tendon-inspired anisotropic surface topography, excellent mechanical properties, anti-inflammatory capacity, and a bioactive ion release gradient, enabling rapid construction of a favorable regenerative microenvironment. In vitro experiments confirmed that the scaffold significantly reduced TNF-α secretion, inhibited macrophage polarization toward the M1 phenotype, promoted the migration, proliferation, and differentiation of tendon stem cells (TSPCs), and enhanced endothelial cell migration, tube formation, and angiogenic factor expression. Meanwhile, in vivo results further demonstrated that the magnesium ion (Mg2+)-loaded anisotropic scaffold significantly increased the M2 macrophages proportion and IL-10 expression, while markedly reducing tissue adhesion. Moreover, endogenous tendon regeneration was significantly enhanced, as evidenced by activation of the HIF1-α/VEGF pathway, a clearly visible vascular network within the tissue, significantly improved proliferation and differentiation capabilities of TSPCs, abundant and well-aligned collagen expression, and substantially enhanced mechanical properties. By integrating the physiological tendon regeneration processes, this biomimetic multifunctional scaffold offers a promising strategy for accelerating tendon regeneration.

articles.title: Bioactive shape-memory biodegradable biliary stent functionalized with dHAM-Curcumin for improved biliary repair and microenvironment modulation.
articles.abstract: NA: Anastomotic stricture after biliodigestive reconstruction remains a clinical challenge leading to recurrent cholangitis, jaundice, and secondary biliary cirrhosis. Conventional plastic stents provide temporary support but are prone to biofilm formation and biliary sludge accumulation and require secondary removal procedures. There is a need for biodegradable biliary stents that provide sufficient mechanical support while actively modulating the local microenvironment. A biodegradable shape-memory biliary stent composed of a poly(CL-co-TOSUO)/BaSO4 (PCT/BaSO4) composite core coated with a decellularized human amniotic membrane-curcumin (dHAM-Cur) hydrogel was developed. In vivo performance was assessed in rat subcutaneous and duodenal implantation models and in a rabbit orthotopic common bile duct stenting model. Gut microbiota and bile metabolomic changes were analyzed by 16S rRNA sequencing and untargeted Liquid Chromatography-Mass Spectrometry (LC-MS). The PCT/BaSO4 stent exhibited suitable mechanical properties, radiopacity, and shape memory functionality, with a degradation profile that matched the expected biliary healing period. The dHAM-Cur coating increased surface hydrophilicity and supported sustained curcumin release. The functionalized stent reduced inflammatory cell infiltration, fibrous capsule formation, and bile duct fibrosis, and preserved biliary patency compared with plastic and PCL/BaSO4 controls in vivo. Multi-omics analyses suggested that the stent subtly reshaped gut microbial composition and modulated bile acid-related metabolic pathways. The PCT/BaSO4@dHAM-Cur composite demonstrated local anti-inflammatory and anti-adhesion effects in preclinical models, along with favorable biocompatibility and anti-restenotic potential. This system holds promise as a therapeutic platform for the clinical management of biliodigestive anastomoses.

articles.title: Cytochalasin D-induced cytoskeletal remodeling with MYH9 enhances release of extracellular vesicles for therapeutic application.
articles.abstract: NA: Extracellular vesicles (EVs) hold great potential as therapeutic vehicles, but their clinical application is limited by low production yields. Here, we explored whether the pharmacological disruption of the actin cytoskeleton using cytochalasin D (CytoD) could enhance EV release while maintaining properties essential for therapeutic use. We examined monocytic U937 cells and colorectal cancer SW480 cells, discovering that CytoD increased EV production by approximately 8.27-fold in U937 cells and 10.06-fold in SW480 cells, while largely preserving the size distribution and surface charge of the EVs. Density gradient ultracentrifugation and label-free quantitative proteomics revealed that CytoD not only increased overall EV release but also selectively remodeled EV proteins. Notably, CytoD-EVs retained lineage-associated membrane proteins such as LFA-1 and showed an enrichment of cytoskeleton-related regulators, particularly MYH9, as well as proteins involved in adhesion and membrane trafficking. We observed the recruitment of MYH9 to membrane blebs,and both pharmacological inhibition with blebbistatin and MYH9 knockdown suppressed EV release, indicating that actomyosin-dependent contractility stimulates EV shedding. Importantly, CytoD-EVs proved to be highly effective drug carriers that doxorubicin-loaded EVs efficiently delivered cargo to recipient cells and induced greater cytotoxicity than free doxorubicin at equivalent doses. Overall, these findings demonstrate that CytoD-induced cytoskeletal remodeling enhances EV production through MYH9-associated membrane dynamics while preserving their capacity for therapeutic delivery. Thus, our findings establish CytoD-induced EV biogenesis as a robust, scalable, and translationally applicable platform for advanced EV-based drug delivery systems.

articles.title: Achieving the targeted retention of nanomotors via a controllable "braking" mechanism based on molecularly programmed engine disassembly.
articles.abstract: NA: Nanomotors have unique autonomous mobility capabilities, offering significant advantages for promoting deep penetration of drugs into pathological sites. However, achieving on-demand "braking" and active retention within target areas remains a critical challenge for efficient, intelligent delivery. The absence of controllable braking mechanisms may cause the nanomotor to continue moving and rapidly dissipate after reaching the target site, hindering effective local enrichment and sustained therapy. In this study, a peptide nucleic acid (PNA)-triggered, in vivo-controlled, engine-disassembly-based active braking mechanism is proposed for nanomotors. This nanomotor anchors the different catalytic engine (catalase, urease, glucose oxidase, and Pt) to the carrier surface via programmable PNA complementary, thus accommodating various application scenarios. After reaching the target area and achieving deep penetration, the injected exogenous complementary chains competitively displace the engine, triggering precise "braking." This braking mechanism relies on PNA sequence-specific base-complementary pairing and competitive displacement, enabling on-demand braking in vivo. Experimental results demonstrate that the drug-loaded nanomotor exhibits excellent tumor-targeting accumulation and tissue penetration capabilities in tumor-bearing mouse models. Following the intravenous injection of PNA to trigger braking, it produces the strongest tumor suppression effect. This study provides a novel strategy for developing intelligent nanomotor therapeutic systems that combine deep penetration with long-lasting retention capabilities.

articles.title: Reprogramming tumor vasculature: Integrating normalization biology with vascularized tumor-on-chip models.
articles.abstract: NA: Abnormal tumor vasculature is a hallmark of the tumor microenvironment that promotes hypoxia, therapeutic resistance, and disease progression while limiting the delivery of anticancer therapy. Although early anti-angiogenic therapies were designed to starve tumors by eliminating their blood supply, excessive vessel pruning often aggravated hypoxia and selected for more aggressive phenotypes. These observations led to the concept of vascular normalization, whereby judicious modulation of angiogenic signaling transiently restores vessel structure and function, improving perfusion, oxygenation, drug delivery, and anti-tumor immunity. In this review, we discuss the mechanisms governing tumor vessel formation, maturation, and dysfunction, and examine therapeutic strategies aimed at normalizing the tumor vasculature. We further highlight the major challenges limiting clinical translation, including the transient and heterogeneous nature of the normalization window, adaptive resistance mechanisms, and the lack of robust tools for longitudinal monitoring. We then integrate vascular normalization biology with vascularized tumor-on-chip platforms, examining how key features of the tumor microenvironment, including tissue architecture, extracellular matrix remodeling, hemodynamic forces, metabolic gradients, and multicellular interactions, can be recreated and quantitatively monitored. We critically evaluate how engineering design, biomaterial selection, vascularization strategies, perfusion, and integrated sensing influence the ability of these platforms to capture vascular normalization and therapeutic responses. By linking the hallmarks of vascular normalization to measurable on-chip phenotypes, vascularized tumor-on-chip systems provide controlled frameworks for investigating resistance mechanisms, optimizing treatment timing, and advancing precision oncology. However, challenges related to physiological fidelity, standardization, scalability, and clinical validation continue to limit their broader translation.

articles.title: On-demand biocatalytic dual oxygen spray reprograms the hypoxia-ferroptosis axis to accelerate chronic wound healing.
articles.abstract: NA: Effective clinical management of chronic hypoxic wounds remains challenging due to persistent hypoxic signaling, oxidative stress, and cellular dysfunction. Hypoxia-induced ferroptosis has recently gained attention as a key molecular driver of impaired healing in chronic wounds such as ischemic and diabetic wounds. Herein, a bioinspired self-oxygenating dual spray incorporating silk fibroin, aloe vera mucilage, and hemoglobin in the primary SAH spray and hydrogen peroxide in the secondary Hp spray is developed. Upon application, the dual oxygenation spray (SAH-Hp) triggers peroxide-responsive instantaneous O2 release through the biocatalytic activity of hemoglobin. Localized O2 generation alleviates hypoxia and restores redox and iron homeostasis, thereby interrupting the hypoxia-driven ferroptotic cascade. Mechanistic investigations demonstrate that sustained oxygenation suppresses lipid peroxidation, limits iron overload, and enhances antioxidant defenses through restoration of the GSH-GPX4 antioxidant defense. Consequently, the SAH-Hp spray promotes angiogenic regeneration and tissue repair under pathological hypoxic conditions. Extensive preclinical validation in rabbit ear ischemic wounds and streptozotocin-induced diabetic wounds confirms accelerated healing accompanied by reduced hypoxic stress and ferroptosis regulation. Collectively, the on-demand SAH-Hp spray facilitates localized O2 generation as an effective strategy for managing chronic wounds by targeting the hypoxia-ferroptosis axis, providing a clinically translatable oxygenation platform for next-generation regenerative wound therapies.

articles.title: A mechanically active microneedle platform integrated with engineered exosomes for enhanced tendon-bone regeneration.
articles.abstract: NA: Functional regeneration of the tendon-bone interface remains a major challenge because early healing is constrained by an adverse inflammatory microenvironment and insufficient mechanical cues. Here, we developed a mechano-regenerative strategy that combines YAP-primed engineered exosomes with localized biomaterial-based delivery and active mechanical stimulation. Exosomes derived from a YAP agonist (PY-60) preconditioned TDSCs (P-Exo) showed enhanced uptake and promoted the osteogenic and chondrogenic differentiation of bone marrow mesenchymal stem cells, accompanied by activation of YAP-associated signaling and PI3K-Akt-related pathways. To improve local retention, P-Exo were incorporated into a ROS-responsive adhesive hydrogel, which accelerated fibrocartilage formation, bone ingrowth, and biomechanical restoration in a rabbit tendon-bone healing model. To address more complex repair conditions, we engineered a three-layer self-contracting microneedle platform for deep-tissue delivery of P-Exo with concurrent active mechanical stimulation. In an infected rat rotator cuff model, this system reduced bacterial burden and oxidative stress, promoted a reparative macrophage polarization and angiogenesis, and improved tendon-bone structural regeneration, biomechanical strength, and functional recovery. Together, these findings support a therapeutic framework in which engineered exosome signaling and active mechanoregulation act in concert to enhance tendon-bone repair.

articles.title: Hybrid nanovesicle artificial antigen-presenting cells integrate endogenous tumor antigen display with senescence-mimetic erythrocyte membrane-directed splenic T-cell priming.
articles.abstract: NA: Artificial antigen-presenting cells (aAPCs) provide a non-genetic approach to T-cell activation, but their in vivo performance is often limited by predefined peptide-major histocompatibility complex class I (pMHC-I) repertoires and inefficient delivery to secondary lymphoid organs. Here, we engineer senescence-derived hybrid nanovesicles that integrate endogenous antigen display and organ-directed trafficking within a single membrane material. Nanovesicles derived from senescent cancer cells retain increased levels of endogenously generated pMHC-I complexes, whereas nanovesicles derived from senescence-mimetic red blood cells confer spleen-directed biodistribution. Fusion of these membranes generates SS-hNVs, which are further functionalized with anti-CD28 and interleukin-2 to form SS-aAPCs that provide coordinated T-cell receptor (TCR), costimulatory, and cytokine signals. Hybrid membrane composition governs splenic accumulation and CD8+ T-cell engagement following intravenous administration. SS-aAPCs expand antigen-specific CD8+ T cells and TCF-1+PD-1+ progenitor-like populations, enhance cytotoxic responses, and suppress tumor growth in B16-OVA and MC38 models. Combination with programmed death-ligand 1 (PD-L1) blockade further improves tumor control. By assigning endogenous antigen display and lymphoid trafficking to distinct source membranes, this platform establishes a structure-function strategy for constructing systemically administered aAPCs. These findings support that physiologically remodeled membranes can be assembled as modular biomaterials to coordinate molecular immune signaling with organ-level biodistribution, enabling in vivo T-cell priming without predefined epitope loading or genetic modification of immune cells.

articles.title: Programming hemostasis and healing via charge-density modulation in a thermo-responsive hydrogel.
articles.abstract: NA: Uncontrolled bleeding and impaired healing are two interlinked challenges in wound management. Here, we introduce charge-density modulation of polymers as a universal design strategy to program biointerfaces that actively promote both hemostasis and healing. By tuning the cationic density of ε-polylysine, we develop an intermediate variant (EPL-C2) that preferentially interacts with fibrinogen over abundant plasma-protein competitors, as supported by protein-adsorption assays, LC-MS/MS analysis, and isothermal titration calorimetry. Incorporating EPL-C2 into a thermo-responsive hydrogel (FN-C2) creates a hemostatic interface that enhances fibrinogen adsorption and platelet adhesion while avoiding broad or excessive activation of the plasma coagulation cascade, leading to superior hemostatic performance in vitro and in a severe arterial injury model. A key advantage of this charge-optimized FN-C2 platform is its ability to serve as a matrix for integrated therapeutic delivery without compromising its hemostatic interface. By loading insulin, the obtained FN-C2-I formulation facilitates sustained release and significantly accelerates skin and intestinal wound healing through enhanced granulation tissue formation, collagen deposition, and a pro-healing immune response. This work presents a synergistic structure-function strategy for next-generation wound dressings, in which tailored control of charge density creates a fibrinogen-selective hemostatic interface inherently compatible with integrated therapeutic delivery.

articles.title: Bimetallic biomimetic catalytic STING sensitizer for coordinating innate and adaptive immune responses against biofilm infections.
articles.abstract: NA: Implant-related infections remain refractory because bacterial biofilms create a physical barrier and are accompanied by local immune dysfunction. Here, we develop a biomimetic metallo-immunocatalytic nanoplatform by cloaking a pH-responsive manganese-iron layered double hydroxide (MFH) core with an M1 macrophage membrane to form MFHM. This design integrates a structurally coupled Mn-Fe catalytic lattice with a functionally preserved biointerface, enabling infection-targeted delivery, colloidal stability, and microenvironment-responsive ion release. Within the acidic biofilm niche, the electronically coupled MFH core promotes Fe/Mn redox cycling and sustains Fenton-like reactive oxygen species generation, thereby disrupting extracellular polymeric substances, damaging bacterial membranes, and perturbing bacterial metal homeostasis. Concurrently, released Mn2+ and redox-active Fe species act as immunomodulatory cues that enhance cyclic GMP-AMP synthase-stimulator of interferon genes (cGAS-STING) and nuclear factor κB (NF-κB) signaling, promote pro-inflammatory macrophage polarization and phagocytic function, and facilitate dendritic-cell maturation and downstream adaptive immune engagement. In a methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus implant-associated infection model, MFHM markedly reduces bacterial burden, promotes tissue repair, and elicits a coordinated immune response that may support protective adaptive immunity, without apparent treatment-related systemic toxicity. These findings establish a catalytic-immune framework based on a biomimetic bimetallic nanostructure and highlight its potential therapeutic application in recalcitrant biofilm-associated infections.

articles.title: Spontaneous phase separation-driven Janus hydrogel spatiotemporally orchestrates the fibrotic progression for functional tendon regeneration.
articles.abstract: NA: Postoperative tendon regeneration hinges on the precise spatiotemporal orchestration of fibrotic progression, aberrant fibrogenesis instead drives pathological adhesion formation and impairs functional recovery. However, current strategies often target isolated aspects of fibrotic progression and rely on complex fabrication procedures. Here, we engineer a Janus hydrogel (SPS-JH) via spontaneous phase separation-driven stratification and photopolymerization of methacrylated hyaluronic acid (HAM) and poly(lactide)-b-poly(propylene glycol)-b-poly(lactide) dimethacrylate (PLD). This innate water/oil demixing yields a Janus architecture in which the outer HAM layer establishes a lubricated anti-adhesion interface, while the inner PLD layer confers durable mechanical reinforcement. Critically, the SPS-JH decodes the temporal hierarchy of tendon repair: the MMP-2-degradable HAM layer releases COX-2 siRNA to silence fibroblast hyperactivation during early inflammation, whereas the PLD matrix sustains niclosamide (NEN) release to polarize macrophages during inflammation and suppress fibrogenesis during proliferation. In rats with Achilles tendon injury, SPS-JH reduces peritendinous adhesions and promotes biomechanically competent, functional tendon regeneration. Transcriptomic analysis reveals coordinated activation of mechanotransduction and tissue remodeling programs accompanied by suppressed fibrogenic signaling. This work establishes a structurally minimalist yet biologically sophisticated paradigm wherein spontaneous phase separation coordinates with the dynamic fibrotic progression to enable functional tendon regeneration.

articles.title: Engineering biomaterials to improve cytokine therapies for wound healing.
articles.abstract: NA: Recombinant cytokines have been used as therapeutics for cancers, autoimmune diseases, and infectious diseases, but their application in wound healing and tissue regeneration remains relatively underdeveloped. Short half-lives, narrow therapeutic windows, and a myriad of adverse effects due to pleiotropy and redundancy have limited their clinical use. Biomaterial-based delivery platforms such as hydrogels, particles, and scaffolds have gained traction as engineering strategies to bridge this translational gap. Despite their popularity in preclinical research, the last FDA approved biomaterial-based cytokine therapeutic, becaplermin, was approved in 1997. Unlike reviews that focus on material design alone, we investigate clinical trials from 2012 to present day and look at the barriers and bottlenecks of translating this technology beyond the bench. This review focuses on release kinetics, design parameters, and practical applications of cytokine-loaded hydrogels, particles, and scaffolds to accelerate wound healing and regenerate functional tissue after soft tissue damage. We offer insights about future directions for preclinical testing and further engineering considerations to aid in their translation to clinical care for patients with soft tissue injuries.

articles.title: Thermosensitive and tumor-targeted asparaginase fusion protein enables metabolic-immunotherapy for solid tumors.
articles.abstract: NA: Metabolic therapies targeting tumor amino acid dependence, represented by asparaginase (ASNase), have shown limited efficacy in solid tumors, owing to poor stability, low penetration, and high immunogenicity. Here, we design a thermosensitive tumor-targeted ASNase fusion protein (ASNase-ELP-LHRH) via AlphaFold2, by integrating elastin-like polypeptide (ELP) and luteinizing hormone-releasing hormone (LHRH), to overcome these drawbacks. ELP drives in situ depot formation, extending half-life to ∼400 h (95-fold increase) and reducing anti-ASNase antibody levels 70-fold. LHRH mediates receptor-dependent tumor targeting and deep penetration. ASNase-ELP-LHRH achieves persistent asparagine (Asn) depletion, counteracting metabolic adaptation to induce nutrient starvation and apoptosis. Mechanistically, the construct blocks metastasis by suppressing epithelial-mesenchymal transition through downregulating Twist1 and upregulating E-cadherin, effectively inhibiting lung metastasis for 25 days in triple-negative breast cancer models. We further observed time-dependent changes in CD8+ T-cell effector-marker expression under Asn deprivation, characterized by dynamic alterations in IFN-γ and granzyme B expression. Combined with anti-PD-L1, this achieves a "dual boost" of antitumor immunity, durably inhibiting metastasis for 40 days and extending survival 1.5-fold. The modular ligand-exchangeable platform offers a generalizable strategy for protein optimization and establishes ASNase-ELP-LHRH as a promising metabolic-immunotherapeutic agent for solid tumors, bridging protein engineering, tumor metabolism and cancer immunology.

articles.title: Rare-earth-free magnesium-zinc alloy with controlled biodegradation and biocompatibility for novel biodegradable metallic stent.
articles.abstract: NA: Biodegradable magnesium (Mg) alloy stents offer a transient alternative to permanent metallic implants; however, clinically used WE43 contains rare-earth (RE) elements, raising concerns regarding the long-term biosafety of RE-containing degradation products and their potential tissue accumulation. Here, we investigated two RE-free Mg-Zinc (Zn)-based alloys, MZ01 (Mg-1Zn-0.1Ca) and ZM115 (Mg-1Zn-1.5Mn-0.5Sr), and established a mechanistic cascade linking alloy composition and microstructure to electrochemical analyses revealed alloy-dependent differences in grain structure and interfacial corrosion resistance, with MZ01 exhibiting the highest charge-transfer resistance. In a mouse subcutaneous model, MZ01 showed more uniform degradation, smaller and more rapidly resolving hydrogen gas cavities, and a significantly lower microcrack area fraction at Day 56 than WE43 and ZM115, accompanied by attenuated inflammatory and fibrotic responses. In the rabbit iliac arteries, all stents maintained luminal patency without thrombosis through 56 days, while MZ01 exhibited lower neointimal thickness, lower perivascular apoptosis and late inflammation, and enhanced early endothelialization compared with WE43. Preliminary descriptive porcine coronary implantation further demonstrated the technical feasibility and sustained patency of MZ01 over 56 days. Collectively, these findings define a composition-microstructure-corrosion-cellular response-vascular healing axis and identify MZ01 as a RE-free Mg-Zn alloy with controlled biodegradation and favorable biocompatibility, supporting its further development as a biodegradable cardiovascular scaffold.

articles.title: Self-assembly prodrugs for controlled singlet oxygen release and resistance modulation in deep-tumor photodynamic therapy.
articles.abstract: NA: Photodynamic therapy (PDT) offers spatiotemporally controlled tumor ablation via photosensitizer-mediated singlet oxygen (1O2) generation, yet its application to deep-seated solid tumors remains fundamentally constrained by limited light penetration and tumor hypoxia. Endoperoxides (EPOs), which reversibly capture and release 1O2, offer a promising strategy to overcome these constraints. Nevertheless, existing EPO-based systems suffer from uncontrolled half-life-dependent 1O2 release and inefficient utilization. Moreover, PDT-induced oxidative stress upregulates inducible nitric oxide synthase (iNOS), leading to nitric oxide (NO) overproduction that quenches 1O2 and promote adaptive resistance. Herein, we report a self-assembly nano-prodrug enabling on-demand 1O2 release while suppressing NO-mediated resistance. An amphiphilic prodrug, L-NARG-SS-Py, comprising a 1O2-storing pyridone moiety and an iNOS inhibitor linked via a glutathione-responsive disulfide bond, co-assembles with protoporphyrin IX to form nano-prodrug (PPIX@L-NARG-SS-Py NPs). Upon irradiation, generated 1O2 is captured and stored as EPO intermediates, followed by glutathione-triggered release in tumor microenvironment. Simultaneously, released iNOS inhibitor suppresses NO production, thereby reducing 1O2 quenching and amplifying oxidative damage. In deep-seated pancreatic tumor models, the nano-prodrug achieves potent tumor suppression with minimal systemic toxicity. This work establishes a biologically amplified, light-independent PDT strategy for overcoming physical and adaptive resistance in deep-tissue phototherapy.

articles.title: Genetically engineering mast cells as effectors for targeted cancer cell cytotoxicity.
articles.abstract: NA: Type-I hypersensitivity is a mast cell-mediated degranulation process induced by IgE-antigen recognition. Inspired by this highly specific mechanism, we developed a new cell therapy platform by genetically engineering mouse mast cell line MC/9 to overexpress the cytotoxic proteins perforin and granzyme B (PG-MCs) via lentiviral transduction. In the melanoma model utilizing B16 cells expressing membrane-bound OVA, a polarized degranulation of mast cells towards cancer cells was validated upon the recognition of antigens by anti-OVA IgE. PG-MCs could selectively kill cancer cells via IgE-antigen recognition. The IgE-sensitized PG-MCs administered through an intertumoral route delivered perforin 1 (Prf1) and granzyme B (Gmzb) toward target cells to potentiate anti-tumor efficacy. Moreover, we demonstrated the reprogramming effect of tumor microenvironment by PG-MC-induced hypersensitivity, driving an immune remodeling of the tumor milieu, characterized by the increased lymphocyte infiltration. In addition, this mast cell therapy, in combination with 5- fluorouracil (5-Fu), induced a significant inhibition of tumor growth in a B16-OVA mouse model, which is associated with the depletion of myeloid-derived suppressor cells (MDSCs).

articles.title: Spatial lipidome and transcriptome profiling reveals stratified lipid architecture in human articular cartilage.
articles.abstract: NA: Lipids, as a class of endogenous biomaterials, are essential for regulating tissue properties and homeostasis. Articular cartilage is an anisotropic tissue that exhibits spatially organized tissue functions and lipid metabolism, and its microenvironment is sensitive to lipid-mediated regulation. However, the spatial lipid composition and its functional significance in cartilage pathophysiology remain elusive. In this study, we performed spatial lipidomic and transcriptomic analyses on healthy and diseased human articular cartilage. We demonstrate a layer-dependent lipid composition mainly in the extracellular matrix and chondrocyte region, and the stratified lipid architecture aligns with region-specific gene expression and cellular phenotypes. The tissue near the cartilage surfaces is enriched with phospholipids and genes relevant to matrix secretion and lipid transport, whereas the tissue adjacent to subchondral bone, is featured by lyso-phospholipids and genes related to biomineralization. Moreover, we highlight ceramide (CER)'s role in mediating chondrocyte secretion and its potential protective function in early osteoarthritis (OA), suggesting that location-specific lipid diversity may contribute to the regulation of cartilage function.
