This study not only advances understanding of cartilage pathophysiology, but also provides a material-level blueprint for developing more biomimetic cartilage engineering strategies.

articles.title: Molecularly nanoengineered dendritic cells for tumor-specific antigen capture and sono-activatable cytokine-mediated immunotherapy.
articles.abstract: NA: Engineering artificial dendritic cells (DCs) holds great promise for cancer immunotherapy, but achieving spatiotemporally controlled multifunctionality within the immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment remains a challenge. Here, we report a chemically engineered, ultrasound (US)-activatable artificial DCs nanosystem (nDC-M) that mimics the DC-mediated T-cell immunity through a rationally designed molecular assembly. The nDC-M integrates three key functional modules including a semiconducting polymer nanoparticle and interleukin-2 (IL-2) crosslinked by hypoxia-cleavable fragment for on-demand cytokine release upon US trigger, a matured DC membrane cloak for tumor cell recognition and a surface-anchored maleimide (MAL) group for covalent antigen capture and presentation. Under US treatment, sonodynamic effect of semiconducting polymer ablates tumors and consumes oxygen to allow breakage of hypoxia-cleavable fragments, leading to IL-2 leakage. This nDC-M exhibits a comprehensive and conferred mimicking functions including tumor cell recognition, antigen presentation and sono-activatable cytokine secretion. In bilateral breast cancer and lung metastasis models, US-driven nDC-M therapy significantly suppresses tumor progression and metastasis. Moreover, combining nDC-M with checkpoint blockade achieves complete eradication of local and distant tumors and establishes long-term immunological memory against recurrence. This work presents a modular and stimuli-responsive artificial DC platform that integrates chemical synthesis, molecular nanoengineering, and function modulation, offering a versatile strategy for cancer immunotherapy.

articles.title: Microneedle-guided ultraviolet phototherapy with local calcipotriol delivery for enhanced psoriasis treatment.
articles.abstract: NA: Narrow-band ultraviolet B (NB-UVB) phototherapy is clinically regarded as a first-line treatment for moderate-to-severe plaque psoriasis owing to its high tolerance, broad applicability and easy affordability. However, the therapeutic efficacy of short-wave UV light is limited by poor penetration through the thickened stratum corneum of psoriatic skin, whereas excessive NB-UVB irradiation may provoke cutaneous photodamage. Moreover, NB-UVB administration necessitates trained personnel and frequent hospital visits, resulting in poor patient compliance. Here, we developed microneedles with high UV transmittance (UVMNs) to enhance the transdermal delivery efficiency of NB-UVB, thereby reducing the required irradiation dosage and mitigating the risk of photodamage without compromising therapeutic effect. A vitamin D analog, calcipotriol, was further coated onto the UVMN patch to augment the overall efficacy of the phototherapeutic regimen. After insertion into the skin, the calcipotriol is released from the dissolvable coating within minutes to suppress keratinocyte proliferation, followed by UVMN-guided NB-UVB therapy for regulation of regulatory T/T helper 17 cell balance as well as inhibition of keratinocyte proliferation. The integration of phototherapy and topical therapy effectively ameliorated symptoms in a psoriatic mouse model.

articles.title: A nanostructured gradient Ta-O-F barrier-reservoir coating on 316L stainless steel coordinates anti-infective and osteoregenerative responses.
articles.abstract: NA: Early-stage bacterial infection and inadequate osseointegration remain major causes of failure of orthopedic 316L stainless steel (316L SS) implants. Fluoride-containing surfaces can provide antibacterial activity and support angiogenic and osteoblastic responses when fluoride exposure is appropriately regulated. However, uncontrolled release may cause burst exposure, compromised cytocompatibility, and limited functional durability. Herein, a nanostructured gradient Ta-O-F coating was constructed on 316L SS by stepwise plasma modification: an outer Ta2O5-rich region served as a corrosion-stable barrier, whereas an underlying fluoride-containing region functioned as an ion reservoir, thereby suppressing burst fluoride release and sustaining subsequent exposure. Compared with monofunctional coatings, TO/TF showed improved corrosion resistance, moderated fluoride release, and retained antibacterial activity against S. aureus and E. coli. Phenotypic and transcriptomic analyses indicated that the antibacterial response was primarily associated with fluoride-mediated membrane damage, oxidative stress, metabolic disturbance, and suppression of translation-related pathways. The Ta2O5-rich surface may provide an additional but relatively weak contribution through corrosion stabilization and favorable surface physicochemical properties. The regulated coating also enhanced endothelial migration and tube formation, while promoting osteoblastic adhesion, proliferation, ALP activity, matrix mineralization, and related gene expression in vitro. In an infected rat implantation model, TO/TF reduced local inflammatory infiltration and bacterial burden relative to unmodified 316L SS, while supporting vascular and osteogenic marker expression and improved peri-implant bone architecture. These findings establish a barrier-reservoir strategy for coordinating early anti-infective protection with subsequent osteoregenerative responses on metallic implants.

articles.title: Cryogenic sintering decellularized tissue particles creates porous scaffolds that support long-term alternative macrophage infiltration in large traumatic injuries.
articles.abstract: NA: Decellularized extracellular matrix (ECM) biomaterials are widely utilized in soft tissue reconstruction, triggering a Type 2 inflammatory response that promotes repair. However, it remains challenging to manipulate the geometry and porosity of native ECM forms, like sheets and particulates, without chemically altering composition. We describe a controlled freeze-drying method to cryogenically sinter ECM particles into large, mechanically stable, porous 3D ECM scaffolds without altering matrix composition. Modulating small intestinal submucosa (SIS) ECM particle concentration (50 to 200 mg/mL) and freezing rate (-30 °C to -196 °C) during sintering enabled control over 3D porosity (934-3476 μm2 pore area). Moderate ECM concentrations (100 mg/mL) and slow freezing rates (-80 °C) created scaffolds with the largest pores and high mechanical stability under large strain (storage modulus 4036 ± 172 Pa). In vivo, scaffolds bridged volumetric muscle and fat pad deficits, with fabrication conditions affecting degradation and immune response between 1 and 18 weeks. Rapid CD206+ macrophage infiltration occurred, particularly in 100 mg/mL -80 °C scaffolds (4752 ± 1773 macrophages/mm2). All ECM forms induced interleukin-4 (Il4) expression during the first 2 weeks (over 10-fold vs untreated), though expression in 100 mg/mL -80 °C scaffolds persisted substantially longer (8 weeks) than non-sintered particles. Small-pored 100 mg/mL -196 °C scaffolds degraded faster and remodeled into adipose tissue after 8 to 18 weeks. This study shows that ECM particulate can be processed into mechanically robust 3D scaffolds with controllable porosity and degradation without altering biochemical composition, influencing Type 2 immune activation and tissue remodeling after volumetric injury.

articles.title: 3D-bioprinted dual-factor nerve conduits promote neurovascular co-regeneration via activation of the PI3K/AKT and MAPK/ERK pathways.
articles.abstract: NA: Peripheral nerve repair across challenging defects remains a major clinical hurdle, partly because conventional nerve guidance conduits fail to reconstruct the neurovascular microenvironment essential for coordinated regeneration. To overcome this, we engineered a 3D-bioprinted multichannel conduit composed of alginate (Alg), gelatin methacryloyl (GelMA), and bacterial nanocellulose (BNC), incorporating separately prepared nerve growth factor (NGF)- and vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF)-loaded poly(lactic-co-glycolic acid) (PLGA) nanospheres and Schwann-like cells derived from stem cells from human exfoliated deciduous teeth (SC-SHEDs). The conduit was evaluated in a 10-mm rat sciatic nerve defect. Combined NGF/VEGF stimulation was associated with sustained AKT and ERK phosphorylation over the measured in vitro time course, together with changes in mTOR and c-Jun phosphorylation. The selected formulation retained the intended printed geometry, supported short-term cell viability, and enabled sustained release of both factors. Across the 1- and 3-month assessments, the NGF + VEGF + SC-SHED group showed increased microvessel density, stronger S100β- and NF200-associated signals, improved myelin morphometry, better electrophysiological and sensorimotor outcomes, and greater gastrocnemius muscle preservation than the untreated control. The combined conduit generally produced the most favorable outcomes among the engineered groups and approached the autograft group for several endpoints. These findings support further evaluation of this integrated strategy for peripheral nerve reconstruction.

articles.title: Polymeric and metallic occluders for interventional therapy of cardiovascular diseases.
articles.abstract: NA: Interventional therapy has, as a minimally invasive approach, been widely adopted for treating cardiovascular diseases, particularly structural heart disease, where occluders play a pivotal role in transcatheter closure. This paper comprehensively reviews the evolutionary trajectory and emerging frontiers of cardiovascular occluders, beginning with their interventional applications in congenital heart defects (atrial septal defect, ventricular septal defect, patent foramen ovale, and patent ductus arteriosus) and left atrial appendage closure. The focus then shifts to occluder materials and design principles, tracing the progression from early non-degradable metals like stainless steel to the current gold standard, nitinol, whose hyperelasticity enables self-expanding devices. To promote rapid endothelialization on nitinol implants, surface nanocoatings of bioceramics such as titanium nitride have been developed to modulate cell-material interactions. To eliminate risks from permanent metallic implants, biodegradable occluders have emerged as an alternative. The design of biodegradable occluders utilizing medical polymers such as polylactic acid and polydioxanone is illustrated, highlighting structural innovations such as locking strategies to overcome the lack of hyperelasticity. Key considerations including matching degradation rate with tissue regeneration and achieving X-ray visibility are also described. Finally, future perspectives are presented: expanding applications to infants and the elderly, incorporating tissue engineering for in situ regeneration, and leveraging nanotechnology and artificial intelligence to optimize device performance. The ongoing advancement of occluder technologies will propel interventional therapy for structural heart disease toward a safer and more effective treatment.

articles.title: From biomarkers to therapeutic targets: Biomaterial-mediated cfDNA scavenging in inflammation.
articles.abstract: NA: Cell-free DNA (cfDNA) displays disease-dependent changes in abundance, fragmentation, composition, and tissue origin. Beyond serving as a noninvasive biomarker, persistent cfDNA can act as a damage-associated molecular pattern, activating TLR9, cGAS-STING, inflammasome signaling, and thromboinflammation. This review synthesizes advances in cfDNA biology, clinical applications, and therapeutic scavenging across inflammatory diseases. We critically evaluate the extent to which current clinical studies support diagnostic, prognostic, and causal conclusions while considering methodological heterogeneity. Particular emphasis is placed on how biomaterials transform cfDNA recognition into treatment. We trace the evolution from free nucleases and soluble cationic agents to nanostructured platforms that integrate DNA sequestration with retention, degradation, lesion targeting, or immunomodulation. Comparison of cationic polymers, dendrimers, core-shell nanoparticles, hydrogels, microneedles, nanosheets, and nuclease-enabled systems reveals how material architecture governs cfDNA accessibility, stability in biofluids, tissue distribution, and therapeutic efficacy. Localized and stimuli-responsive designs may improve selectivity and reduce systemic toxicity, but most efficacy evidence remains preclinical. Clinical translation therefore requires standardized cfDNA measurement, realistic biofluid testing, rigorous pharmacology, scalable manufacturing, and prospective demonstration that selective cfDNA removal improves outcomes without compromising host defense.

articles.title: A tunable brain-targeted PEGylated ginsenoside Rg1 derivative disrupts the ROS-mediated inflammasome-pyroptosis cascade to ameliorate Alzheimer's cognitive deficits.
articles.abstract: NA: The pathogenic cascade of oxidative stress, neuroinflammation, and pyroptosis serves as a core driving factor in the pathogenesis and progression of Alzheimer's disease (AD). Although ginsenoside Rg1 exhibits pleiotropic neuroprotective activities, its poor blood-brain barrier (BBB) permeability severely hinders its clinical translation. To overcome this limitation, a brain-targeted delivery system was constructed using a covalent conjugation strategy, linking purified Rg1 with rhodamine B-modified polyethylene glycol (PEG) of varying chain lengths (Rg1s-PEG). After screening, the derivative Rg1s-PEG-600 was identified as achieving an optimal balance between hydrophilic stealth properties and steric hindrance, demonstrating enhanced brain accumulation and favorable biosafety profiles. In both in vitro and in vivo models of lipopolysaccharide-induced acute neuroinflammation, Rg1s-PEG-600 attenuated reactive oxygen species (ROS) accumulation, inhibited canonical neuronal pyroptosis mediated by the NLRP1/3 inflammasomes, and significantly ameliorated behavioral deficits and synaptic loss. Furthermore, in chronic 5xFAD transgenic mice, systemic administration of Rg1s-PEG-600 for 12 weeks markedly reversed spatial memory decline, anxiety-like behavior, and synaptic protein depletion. Mechanistic studies further revealed that this targeted nanotherapeutic not only suppressed the ROS-NLRP1 signaling axis and subsequent neuronal pyroptosis in the AD brain but also comprehensively inhibited amyloidogenesis and Tau hyperphosphorylation. This work provides a promising, multitarget nanotherapeutic strategy to overcome BBB limitations and disrupt the complex pathological networks underlying neurodegenerative diseases.

articles.title: Implanted and degradable hydrogel evaporative cooler for regional and repeated mild hypothermia therapy of traumatic brain injury.
articles.abstract: NA: Implantable, regional and repeated mild hypothermia represents a promising therapeutic strategy for traumatic brain injury. Here, we develop a soft, degradable hydrogel microchannel evaporative cooler capable of removing heat through water evaporation in microchannels and achieving focused regional cooling within a short time. Fabricated from degradable hydrogels and using water as the coolant, the cooler shows biocompatibility and tissue adhesion. In vivo intracranial experiments with the cooler adhered on the rat dura mater enabled precise temperature regulation during repeated regional hypothermia (33 ± 0.5 °C, 4 h per day for 3 consecutive days). The treatment conferred neuroprotection and supported neural repair, with therapeutic effects persisting for 14 days. Sustained recovery was associated with increased Nestin+/Ki67+ and Sox2+/Ki67+ cells, along with elevated MAP2/PSD95 co-localization. Additional staining confirmed the presence of Nestin+/GFAP- and Sox2+/GFAP- cell populations, supporting the involvement of progenitor-like cells. At 28 days post-injury, rats receiving treatment exhibited reduced lesion volume, preserved axonal integrity and myelination, and ameliorated cognitive performance. Proteomic profiling performed at day 3 further suggested that repeated hypothermia modulates synaptic plasticity, dampens neuroinflammation, and rescues perturbed energy metabolism, representing a multi-faceted response distinct from single-episode hypothermia. Collectively, these findings highlight the translational potential of this implantable cooling strategy for TBI therapy.

articles.title: Dual immuno-mechanical programming of a biomimetic periosteum for load-bearing bone restoration.
articles.abstract: NA: Age-related cortical bone loss remains a major clinical challenge, as current interventions largely neglect the load-bearing cortex and its periosteal niche. Here, a dual-targeted biomimetic periosteum is engineered by mechanistically decoding how inflammaging and mechanical decline converge to impair periosteal stem/progenitor cell (PSC) function. Aging-associated macrophage polarization toward a pro-inflammatory M1 state suppresses Piezo1 expression in PSCs, whereas reduced mechanical input attenuates Piezo1 activation, jointly leading to defective mechanotransduction and osteogenesis. Guided by this mechanoinflammatory framework, a periosteum-mimetic membrane is rationally designed with two complementary modules. First, 2-N,6-O-sulfated chitosan (26SCS) is incorporated to repolarize macrophages and restore Piezo1 expression in PSCs. Second, electrospun fiber architecture is optimized to identify a diameter range that maximally activates Piezo1-dependent Ca2+ influx and YAP signaling under reduced mechanical conditions. This coordinated immunomodulatory-mechanosensory strategy reinstates PSC osteogenic competence and enhances cortical bone thickness and strength in aged and hindlimb-unloaded models. The regenerative effect is abolished in Prrx1+ Piezo1-deficient mice, confirming the necessity of Piezo1-mediated mechanotransduction. This work integrates immune microenvironment regulation with cell-scale mechanosensitive activation, providing a periosteum-targeted biomaterial strategy for rebuilding load-bearing cortical bone during aging and mechanical disuse.

articles.title: Blood-transforming coating enables hemostasis and vascularized bone re-generation via bioactive gelation.
articles.abstract: NA: Conventional bone repair materials often treat blood as an obstacle through physical isolation or passive hemostasis, overlooking its physiological role in the regenerative cascade. Here, we propose a "Blood-Transforming Coating" concept and engineer a functionalized microsphere system (GM/TCP@PEG). The NHS ester-coated microspheres rapidly crosslink with amino-rich blood components to form a robust hydrogel while covalently anchoring to tissue surfaces, transforming blood into a synergistic component that enhances material function. Structural characterization confirmed the core-shell architecture. In in-vitro experiments, the clotting time of GM/TCP@PEG was 15.43 s. Its clotting efficiency index was 4.79-fold that of uncoated microspheres and 15.8-fold that of commercial Yunnan Baiyao (YM). The clot mass was 1.63-fold higher than uncoated microspheres and 2.35-fold higher than commercial Yunnan Baiyao (YM). The shear strength measured on porcine skin reached 25.35 kPa, which was 5.39-fold that of the control group. The blood-derived hydrogel enabled sustained release of VEGF, PDGF-BB, and TGF-β1, promoting endothelial cell migration and tube formation. In vivo, GM/TCP@PEG microspheres achieved rapid hemostasis in rat liver, tail, and porcine liver/spleen hemorrhage models, and significantly enhanced bone regeneration via early vascularization in a rat critical-sized calvarial defect model. This blood-transforming strategy achieves synergistic hemostasis, adhesion, and pro-repair functions, provide a strategy with application prospects for tissue repair in complex hemorrhagic environments.

articles.title: Catalytic MXene implant interfaces reprogram radiation-induced foreign body response to prevent capsular contracture.
articles.abstract: NA: Radiotherapy markedly exacerbates foreign body response (FBR) to silicone implants, driving capsular fibrosis and contracture, yet actionable interfacial mechanisms remain insufficiently defined. Here, we engineer an implant-centered Ti3C2Tx MXene-modified PDMS coating (APM) to modulate the redox microenvironment at the tissue-implant interface to reprogram radiotherapy-induced FBR. Oxygen plasma activation and 3-aminopropyltriethoxysilane (APTES) silanization enable covalent anchoring of single-layer MXene nanosheets onto PDMS, yielding a conformal APM film with enhanced hydrophilicity, preserved layered MXene architecture, enzyme-mimicking ROS-scavenging activity, and excellent cytocompatibility. Transcriptomic profiling guides the study, revealing the coordinated downregulation of inflammatory and extracellular matrix remodeling pathways. Mechanistically, interfacial redox regulation dampens NF-κB signaling and reduces endothelial ICAM-1 expression, thereby limiting monocyte adhesion and downstream inflammatory amplification. A tri-culture endothelial-macrophage-fibroblast model further demonstrates that MXene interfaces disrupt pro-inflammatory crosstalk and inhibit myofibroblast activation. In a murine peri-implant irradiation model, APM-coated implants preserve a CD31+/ICAM-1-low microvasculature, reduce peri-implant pro-inflammatory macrophage accumulation, and significantly decrease capsular thickness and collagen deposition. Collectively, these findings demonstrate that MXene-based catalytic coatings can disrupt the positive feedback loop between radiation injury and fibrotic capsule formation, offering a mechanistically grounded strategy to mitigate implant-associated fibrosis.

articles.title: Ultrasound-triggered spinal cord-mimetic electroactive hydrogel enables localized bioelectrical modulation and promotes spinal cord injury repair through JNK-mediated autophagy.
articles.abstract: NA: Spinal cord injury (SCI) creates a hostile microenvironment that severely limits neural regeneration and functional recovery. Although bioelectrical modulation has emerged as a promising strategy for SCI repair, existing biomaterials generally provide either passive electrical conduction or stimulus-responsive electrical generation, but rarely integrate both properties within a mechanically compliant scaffold suitable for spinal cord repair. Here, we developed an injectable, remotely activatable electroactive hydrogel (SMT) by integrating conductive MXene nanosheets into a silk fibroin/tannic acid matrix, endowing the scaffold with tissue-matched mechanics, continuous electrical conductivity, and stimulus-responsive electrical output. Upon ultrasound activation, SMT generated localized bioelectrical cues within the lesion site. At the cellular level, SMT exhibited intrinsic antioxidant and anti-inflammatory effects that were further enhanced by ultrasound activation, while SMT + US promoted autophagic flux through Ca2+-dependent JNK signaling. In a rat model of SCI, the ultrasound-activated hydrogel promoted neural tissue repair and remyelination, attenuated reactive gliosis, and improved functional recovery. Collectively, this study presents a remotely activatable electroactive hydrogel for SCI repair and provides a promising strategy for dynamic bioelectrical regulation during SCI repair.

articles.title: Regulating the iron-ROS cycle via electronic structure-engineered nanoregulators for Parkinson's disease therapy.
articles.abstract: NA: Iron-driven reactive oxygen species (ROS) amplification forms a self-sustaining pathological cycle in Parkinson's disease (PD), yet remains difficult to therapeutically interrupt due to the lack of strategies that coordinate metal homeostasis and redox regulation. Here, we report an electronic-structure-engineered nanoregulatory strategy that regulates the iron-ROS cycle rather than passively scavenging ROS. Nitrogen-doped, herbal-derived carbon dots (CD) were rationally constructed to establish a conjugated electronic framework, in which heteroatom-induced electron delocalization defined redox-active sites and governed the coupling between iron chelation and catalytic ROS regulation. This structure-electronic state-function relationship enabled programmable disruption of the iron-ROS feedback loop at its source. Functionally, the nanoregulators achieved low-density lipoprotein receptor-related protein 1 (LRP1)-mediated brain delivery, exhibited efficient central nervous system exposure, and underwent brain clearance via the cerebrospinal fluid pathway. At the cellular level, they restored mitochondrial function, suppressed ferroptosis-associated lipid peroxidation, and reprogramed stress-related pathways toward neuronal survival. Transcriptomic analysis further revealed coordinated regulation of redox, metabolic, and inflammatory networks. In Parkinsonian mice, this strategy reduced iron deposition, preserved dopaminergic neurons, and improved motor function. Integration with levodopa further enabled sustained, disease-modifying neuroprotection.

articles.title: Dynamic tensile conditioning of mesenchymal stem cell-laden auxetic scaffolds for enhanced YAP-dependent miR-30 enrichment in extracellular vesicles for pulmonary fibrosis therapy.
articles.abstract: NA: Mesenchymal stem cell-derived extracellular vesicles are promising for treating pulmonary fibrosis. However, the generation of extracellular vesicles (EVs) bearing potent, specific therapeutic cargo remains a significant clinical challenge. This study aims to demonstrate how a material-instructive strategy can be utilized to engineer cargo-specific EVs by precisely mimicking the physiological breathing motion of the lung microenvironment. A dynamic culture system was developed by combining a photo-crosslinkable lung decellularized extracellular matrix with an auxetic scaffold. Mesenchymal stem cells (MSCs) were cultured on these scaffolds under dynamic stretching. The dynamically conditioned EVs (dEVs) were then collected, and their therapeutic mechanisms and efficacy were evaluated both in vitro and in vivo using bleomycin-treated human pulmonary fibroblasts and a bleomycin-induced rat pulmonary fibrosis model, respectively. Dynamic stretching on auxetic scaffolds enhanced MSC mechanotransduction, as indicated by the upregulation and nuclear accumulation of YAP. This mechanical activation drove a YAP-dependent biogenesis pathway, leading to the selective enrichment of miR-30 in dEVs. In vivo administration of dEVs effectively restored lung architecture and attenuated collagen deposition. Mechanistically, dEV-derived miR-30 exerted dual therapeutic effects by directly inhibiting myofibroblast activation and promoting the macrophage phenotype switch from pro-inflammatory M1 to anti-inflammatory M2. Furthermore, the EVs successfully restored mitochondrial homeostasis in damaged cells, thereby supporting tissue repair. EVs engineered with miR-30 mimics fully recapitulated the potent therapeutic effects of dEVs, significantly outperforming miR-100. This study successfully established an auxetic dECM scaffold-based mechanogenetic platform to engineer cargo-specific EVs. The findings indicate that mechanical priming optimizes EV therapeutic efficacy, highlighting the YAP/miR-30 axis and mitochondrial restoration as key targets for alleviating pulmonary fibrosis.

articles.title: Mechanisms underlying biomaterial-regulated macrophage polarization in bone tissue engineering: From interface sensing to immune microenvironment remodeling.
articles.abstract: NA: Traditional biomaterials commonly trigger a foreign body reaction after implantation, leading to fibrous encapsulation and poor osseointegration. Advances in osteoimmunology have enabled contemporary tissue engineering to redefine biomaterials as active modulators of the osteoimmune microenvironment rather than as passive scaffolds. At the core of this reconceptualization is the targeted control of macrophage polarization to establish an immune environment conducive to bone repair. The plasticity of macrophages reflects the dynamic balance between the M1 pro-inflammatory and M2 pro-regenerative states; this plasticity ultimately determines regenerative outcomes. This review offers a conceptual four-dimensional regulatory framework that extends from extracellular interface sensing to intracellular genome remodeling and progresses from material properties and signaling cascade stratification to mitochondrial reprogramming and non-coding RNA (ncRNA) networks. Within this framework, material interfaces function as platforms for activating, transducing, and integrating bioactive signals. These signals can be externally modulated to reshape intracellular metabolic organization and sustain mitochondrial function. At a finer regulatory tier, ncRNAs modulate signaling pathways to achieve the precise post-transcriptional regulation of gene expression. Central to this model is a bidirectional, spatiotemporally dynamic feedback loop linking intrinsic cellular machinery with extrinsic material systems. Linking material design parameters to dynamic biological responses lays a conceptual foundation for the development of biomaterials capable of the adaptive and programmable regulation of the osteoimmune microenvironment. Future research may focus on the precise temporal control of M1/M2 phenotypic switching and the coordinated presentation of multiple signals, thereby advancing the development of next-generation immunomodulatory biomaterials for bone repair.

articles.title: A self-assembled hydrophobic polymer tagged nanoplatform for membrane protein degradation and immunomodulatory drug delivery.
articles.abstract: NA: Targeted protein degradation (TPD) has emerged as a powerful strategy for eliminating disease-driving proteins, yet its broader application remains constrained by limited target specificity and the lack of integrated therapeutic delivery functions. Here, we report Tri@N, a multimodal polymeric nanoplatform that extends hydrophobic polymer-based TPD to membrane-associated targets while simultaneously enabling immunomodulatory drug delivery. Tri@N is engineered to remain stable during systemic circulation but undergo intracellular disassembly in response to elevated GSH levels. This disassembly exposes hydrophobic polymer segments that function as a hydrophobic polymer tag, promoting EGFR destabilization and degradation through both proteasomal and autophagy-lysosomal pathways. In parallel, Tri@N releases niclosamide (NIC), which suppresses the STAT3/PD-L1 signaling axis. In colorectal cancer models, Tri@N achieved coordinated EGFR degradation and PD-L1 downregulation, resulting in enhanced CD8+ T cell-mediated antitumor immunity and robust tumor suppression in vivo. These findings establish Tri@N as a dual-functional polymeric nanoplatform that integrates hydrophobic polymer tagging-mediated degradation of a membrane protein with therapeutic payload delivery, providing a versatile strategy for multimodal cancer therapy.

articles.title: Biomimetic electroactive nano-heterojunction for vascularized bone regeneration in large segmental load-bearing bone defects via temporal regulation of endogenous functional ions.
articles.abstract: NA: The repair and functional reconstruction of large segmental bone defects in load-bearing regions are extremely difficult, mainly because the body's capacity to recruit endogenous functional ions such as Ca2+, Cu2+, and Mg2+ to facilitate mineralization and vascularization is compromised. Herein, inspired by the bioelectric field-mediated ion regulation in native bone, a biomimetic carbon fiber reinforced polyetherketoneketone (CF/PEEK) scaffold incorporated with a bio-heterojunction was fabricated via 3D printing, liquid-phase chemistry and hydrothermal treatment. The heterojunction composed of 2D nano-MXene and in-situ ZnS quantum dots enriches functional ions on the scaffold surface through an endogenous electric field, thereby remarkably improving its bioactivity. In vitro cell experiments demonstrated that the CF/PEEK biomimetic scaffold promotes cells' osteogenic and angiogenic differentiation through the epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR)-mediated phosphatidylinositol 3-kinase (PI3K)/protein kinase B (Akt) signaling pathway. In vivo investigations via non-load-bearing lacunar and load-bearing segmental bone defect models verified that the CF/PEEK biomimetic scaffold possesses superior bone and vascular regeneration capacity, enabling rapid vascularized bone regeneration under complex stress conditions through a bone-vessel coupling mechanism. This work offers a novel strategy for repairing load-bearing large segmental bone defects and new insights into designing bioelectric field-guided biomimetic materials.
